provisional_reason: orchestration/ROADMAP.md is CONDEMNED (CLAUDE.md rule 0b, 2026-08-14): it was written from working memory rather than the repo, missed most of Morrowind's systems, compressed the whole visual programme into one step, and never opened the 49 W1 plans or 211 reference items. It will be DELETED AND REWRITTEN from a coverage audit with a different structure and probably different ids. The items below are a hand-transcription of the condemned file — a FIXTURE for the mechanism, not verified truth about the project. Do not quote pct_done from this file as a real completion estimate until this flag is cleared. The tool (tools/roadmap.mjs) is schema-general and reads whatever roadmap.json contains; the rewritten file is expected to drop in without redispatching this piece.
purpose: Machine-readable form of ROADMAP.md, read by tools/roadmap.mjs. One FLAT list of items, each carrying a `phase` (A-F) rather than a second nesting level — a hierarchy drifts out of sync with a hand-edited document; a flat list with a tag does not. The `state` on every record is a CLAIM copied from the prose; the tool verifies it against `evidence` at run time and downgrades an unverifiable claim to UNVERIFIED rather than trusting this file. Phase B-F items are deliberately `not_started` with `evidence: []` — ROADMAP.md's own words: "resolution deliberately drops with distance ... later phases name the work and its visible outcome but will be re-planned when they come into view." That is not a gap in this tracker; inventing a criterion for them would be worse than leaving them honestly unevidenced.
note_on_evidence: Each evidence entry proves the state CURRENTLY claimed, not the item's eventual closes_when. A `path` entry must exist on disk. A `command` entry must exit with the stated code and, if `contains` is given, its combined stdout+stderr must contain that substring. A `json_field` entry reads a JSON file and checks a top-level (dot-path) key against `one_of`. All commands here are offline, no browser, no GPU pod, and each was timed under 2s when this file was written.
note_on_percentage: ROADMAP.md, verbatim: "Anyone quoting a completion percentage should quote it against this list [all items, Phase A through F], not against Phase A, or it means nothing." tools/roadmap.mjs's headline percentage is against every item in every phase. A Phase A sub-total is also printed, unmistakably labelled as a sub-total — Phase A is the only phase currently planned to step granularity.

items.closes_when: Protocol A is re-run blind against the same plates and we stop losing 5 of 5. Not when the orphan count reaches zero — statistics can fail a build and can never pass one.

items.title: Buildings are not inside each other
items.visible_outcome: Doors open into streets rather than into other buildings.
items.closes_when: The 76 interpenetrating pairs (25 with a door inside another building) are resolved. Resolver work is done: game/src/world/footprint.js is now the single implementation of the collision geometry (there were three private copies, two of which agreed with each other over a rectangle the world does not have, which is why the defect stayed invisible), and the check now correctly reports 76 where the old, wrong check reported 22. Shrinking alone clears only 6 of 76 — the interiors are native records with one centimetre of slack already spent — so the remaining 70 need repositioning at the generator, which is step 2c.

evidence.note: the consolidated single implementation of the rotated-footprint geometry — replaced three disagreeing private copies
the ratchet: exits non-zero if any settlement's overlap count regresses or a new door lands inside a building
the resolver is built and is itself waiting on an independent critic — not self-graded (rule 22)

items.unevidenced_note: The visible outcome ('doors open into streets') is not yet true for all 76 remaining pairs — this item stays in_progress, not done, until step-2c closes.

items.title: Building layout: move the interpenetrating pairs at the generator
items.visible_outcome: The generator does not re-author the same building collisions on every regeneration; the remaining interpenetrating pairs (five Blackrose pairs authored exactly 1.0 m apart; thorn-gate/thorn-house-0 sharing an identical offset_m — not a coincidence) are repositioned at the source rather than hand-patched.
items.closes_when: The generator's placement logic no longer produces colliding offsets for these pairs, and node tools/check-building-overlap.mjs's frozen baseline can be re-frozen lower without any settlement's door-in-building count going up.
items.unevidenced_note: Not yet dispatched — ROADMAP.md places it below step 1 in priority ('step 1 is where the screen changes most'), so there is no builder assigned and nothing to evidence yet. This is the honest not_started case, not a gap in the tracker.
